sources.title: VESA — VESA Releases DisplayPort 2.1 Specification
quotes: VESA certified DP40 cables support up to the UHBR10 link rate (10 Gbps), with four lanes, providing a maximum throughput of 40 Gbps
VESA certified DP80 cables support up to the UHBR20 link rate (20 Gbps), with four lanes, providing a maximum throughput of 80 Gbps.
mandated support for VESA’s visually lossless Display Stream Compression (DSC) codec

sources.title: VESA — DisplayPort UHBR device certification and DP40/DP80 cables
quotes: The higher bandwidths enabled by UHBR support a variety of use cases such as uncompressed 8K 60Hz HDR, 4K 240Hz HDR, two 4K 120Hz HDR or four 4K 60Hz HDR displays through a single cable.
VESA certified DP80 cables will also support the UHBR13.5 link rate (13.5 Gbps)
full-feature passive USB-C cables already support UHBR bit rate speeds

sources.title: VESA DisplayPort — FAQ (DSC, adapters, DisplayPort over USB-C)
quotes: DisplayPort 1.4a supports 8K video at 60Hz and 24-bit color using a low 2:1 compression ratio
It is preferable to use a USB-C to DisplayPort adapter cable, and it is best to use a DP certified adapter cable.
use of such adapter is not recommended because it may result in poor picture quality, intermittent operation, or no video display.
DisplayPort, USB data, and USB Power Delivery can all be carried simultaneously through the same USB Type-C connector and cable.

sources.title: VESA — VESA Brings DisplayPort to New USB Type-C Connector (DisplayPort Alt Mode)
quotes: Using 5.4 Gbps across all four high-speed lanes will support up to 4K (4096 x 2160) display resolutions at a 60Hz frame rate with up to 30-bit color.

the use of two lanes for DisplayPort at 8.1 Gbps per lane would allow simultaneous transfer of SuperSpeed USB data (up to 10 Gbps in each direction) while also supporting a 4K UHD (3840 x 2160) DisplayPort monitor.

When using all four lanes for DisplayPort Alt Mode, which could drive a monitor with up to 5K (5120 x 2880) resolution, USB 2.0 data can still be carried across the USB Type-C connection using separate pins dedicated for that function.
Video source devices that support DisplayPort Alt Mode on a USB Type-C connector can use an appropriate adaptor to drive an HDMI, DVI or VGA display.
